data.why: the repository ships real raw .hex CTD casts, calibration.xmlcon, config.toml and stations.csv for four cruises under cruises/<cruise_id>/, which main.py consumes directly; no synthetic data is needed.

goals: pick a cruise and station and inspect the vertical temperature/salinity/oxygen/chlorophyll profile for a single CTD cast
toggle QC filtering and surface-soak inclusion to see how spike removal and soak elimination change a profile
compare water-mass structure across stations using a T-S (temperature-salinity) diagram with isopycnal contours
view a cross-section plot along a cruise track to see how density/oxygen structure varies between stations
check per-cruise build provenance (calibration SHA-256, git commit, rows written) and per-station summary health stats
export the cleaned, binned CTD data for a station as CSV for further analysis

review.summary: The tree faithfully covers the dashboard's ten tabs as a sensible five-phase workflow of selecting, quality-checking, examining, comparing and exporting, and it honestly notes that build provenance and T-S isopycnals are absent from the UI. It needs small corrections before filing: the AOU node misdescribes what is shaded, the section-contour and filter-scope claims are hedged or overstated, one export screen proves nothing, and the AOU/Φ views have no feature.
